ctx:
Context size (-c): how many tokens the model can hold at once -
prompt + chat history + character card + the reply.

Typical: 8192–32768. Must not exceed what the model was trained
for (shown above as 'train ctx') unless you add RoPE scaling.
KV cache memory grows linearly with this value.
With Parallel > 1 the context is SPLIT between slots.
fit:
Fit: set Context to the largest value that fits in this GPU's
currently FREE VRAM, using all your other settings (KV cache
type, GPU layers, CPU MoE, ubatch, mmproj).

Capped at the model's training context, rounded down to a
multiple of 1024, keeps a safety margin (Settings → Fit margin).
Lower KV cache precision (q8_0) or offload MoE experts first
if you want more context to fit.
SWA models (e.g. Gemma) use less KV than estimated, so you
can usually go higher than Fit suggests.
ngl:
GPU layers (-ngl): how many of the model's layers live on the GPU.

999 = all layers (fastest).
 -1 = auto: llama.cpp measures free VRAM at load time and offloads
      as many layers as fit, keeping the rest in system RAM.
      The most reliable choice when a model doesn't fully fit.
Lower values put layers in system RAM; each one slows generation.
Partial offload still needs GPU room for prompt processing
(the estimate includes it).
For MoE models, prefer 'CPU MoE layers' instead of lowering this.
fa:
Flash attention (-fa): faster, much more memory-efficient attention.

  on    force it (recommended)
  auto  let llama.cpp decide per model/GPU
  off   disable - uses far more VRAM at long context and makes
        quantized K/V cache unusable.

Try 'off' only if a specific model produces garbage with it on.
kv:
KV cache type (-ctk / -ctv).

Precision of the KV cache (the model's memory of the conversation).
Sets both -ctk and -ctv to the same type:

  f16    full quality, 2 bytes/value. Default; use it if it fits.
  q8_0   ~half the size of f16, practically lossless.
         Best choice when you need more context.
  q4_0   ~1/4 the size of f16. Noticeable quality loss on long
         chats and recall of earlier details. Last resort.

Quantized types (q8_0, q4_0) require Flash attn = on/auto.
These matched pairs have fast GPU kernels in a default
llama.cpp build. Other types (q5_x, q4_1, iq4_nl, mixed K/V)
need a build with -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=ON; if you have
one, pass -ctk/-ctv in Extra args to override this setting.
n_cpu_moe:
CPU MoE layers (--n-cpu-moe): MoE models only (Qwen3-30B-A3B,
GPT-OSS, GLM-Air, etc). Keeps the expert weights of the first N
layers in system RAM; attention and everything else stays on GPU.

Because only a few experts run per token, this costs far less speed
than lowering GPU layers. Start at 0, raise until the estimate fits.
No effect on dense (non-MoE) models.
parallel:
Parallel slots (-np): how many requests the server handles at once.

Keep this at 1 for SillyTavern, even with extensions like
Summaryception. With 2+ slots, requests run SIMULTANEOUSLY and
compete for the GPU, PCIe and CPU - a background summary can slow
your chat to a crawl (measured on a model with experts in RAM),
and MTP speed-up mostly disappears.

The context is also divided between slots (-c 16384 -np 2 gives
each 8192) unless --kv-unified is passed.

To stop background requests evicting the chat's cache, use
--cache-ram <MiB> in Extra args instead (if your build has it):
the chat's cache is saved to system RAM and restored afterwards.
threads:
CPU threads (-t): only matters for work done on the CPU (layers
not offloaded, CPU MoE experts).

0 = let llama.cpp choose. If you lean on CPU MoE layers, try your
physical core count (10 on an i9-10850K).
port:
TCP port for this server's API. Each pane needs a different port.
OpenAI-compatible endpoint: http://<host>:<port>/v1
batch:
Logical batch size (-b): max prompt tokens submitted per step.
Only affects prompt processing, not generation speed.

Default 2048 is fine. Must be >= UBatch.
ubatch:
Physical batch size (-ub): prompt tokens actually computed at once
on the GPU.

512 (default) is balanced. 1024–2048 can speed up long prompt
processing but enlarges the compute buffer (watch the estimate).
Must be <= Batch.
dual_toggle:
Dual GPU mode: the left pane loads ONE model across both GPUs.
The right pane is hidden while this is on; both cards' VRAM/busy
monitors show at the top of the left pane. Stop the right pane's
model before turning it on.

Options are saved separately for dual-GPU loads of each model.
dual_strategy:
How to span the model over both GPUs (layer split):

  Auto Balance  both cards end up the same % full. Keeps the smaller
                card away from its limit (where the driver starts
                evicting memory). Recommended.
  Auto Speed    use the larger card alone if it fits (fastest: no
                PCIe hand-off), else put as little as possible on the
                smaller card.
  Auto VRAM     maximum free room on both cards - for the biggest
                model or longest context (Fit uses all of it).
  Manual        choose split mode, ratio and device order yourself.

Layer split gives each card a block of layers: one hand-off per token,
works with mismatched cards. Generation is not faster than one card
(cards work in turn) - the win is capacity. The larger card always gets
the output layer, its big logits buffer and the MTP drafter.
dual_mode:
Split mode (Manual), as supported by your llama-server build:
  layer   blocks of layers per card (robust, any card mix)
  tensor  every weight split across both cards; experimental, syncs
          every layer over PCIe - only worth it on fast links with
          matched cards
  row     older per-row split (removed from recent builds)
  none    one card only (the first device)
dual_ts:
Tensor split ratio (Manual): share of the model for the first and
second device, e.g. 3,7. For layer mode it decides how many layers
each card gets. Blank = proportional to free VRAM.
dual_moe_spread:
Which layers keep their MoE experts in system RAM (CPU MoE layers > 0):

  off  plain --n-cpu-moe: the FIRST layers (default). Measured ~8% faster
       generation and prompts - fewer CPU<->GPU switches per token.
  on   split evenly between both cards' layer ranges, relieving both
       cards' VRAM (uses -ot overrides): ~5k more context on GLM-Air,
       at ~8% lower speed.

Note: either way, during prompt processing llama.cpp streams ALL
RAM-side experts through the FIRST card's PCIe link, so prompt speed
is limited by that link. Bigger UBatch (e.g. 2048) = fewer transfers =
much faster prompts. Generation is computed by the CPU either way.
dual_first:
Device order (Manual): which card gets the FIRST layers. The other
card gets the last layers plus the output layer, logits and MTP
drafter - normally that should be the larger card.
relax_tpl:
Relaxed chat template: allow system messages anywhere in the chat.

Some templates (e.g. Qwen) reject a system message that isn't the
first message ('System message must be at the beginning'), which
breaks SillyTavern Chat Completion presets that inject author's
notes / World Info / post-history instructions as system messages.

When on, the app copies the model's own template, turns that check
into a normal system turn, saves it in ./templates and passes it
with --chat-template-file. Everything else (thinking on/off, tools)
is unchanged. Requires --jinja.
jinja:
--jinja: format chats with the template embedded in the GGUF.

Leave ON. Needed for correct tool calling and reasoning/thinking
handling on most modern models.
mtp:
MTP drafter (speculative decoding helper, e.g. Gemma 4 'mtp-*.gguf').

A small companion model drafts several tokens ahead; the main model
verifies them in one pass. Same output, typically 30-50% faster
generation. Shares the main model's KV cache; costs roughly its
file size in extra VRAM.

Detected from files named *mtp* / *assistant* in the model's folder
or an 'MTP' subfolder. The note below shows whether it matches this
model's size (a 31B drafter only works with 31B models).
Fine-tunes of the same base usually work, with lower acceptance.

(off) disables it. Passes: --model-draft <file> --spec-type draft-mtp
Needs a llama.cpp build from after 2026-06-07.
mtp_n:
Draft max (--spec-draft-n-max): how many tokens the drafter
proposes per step.

4 is the recommended default. Higher helps only when acceptance
is very high (predictable text); lower if acceptance is poor.
Watch 'draft acceptance' in Status after a request.
mmproj:
Vision projector (--mmproj): lets multimodal models see images.

Lists mmproj*.gguf files in the model's folder. Only needed if you
send images; adds a few hundred MB to a few GB of VRAM.
extra:
Extra arguments passed straight to llama-server, shell-style.

Examples:
  --temp 0.7 --min-p 0.05     default sampling (clients usually
                              send their own)
  --reasoning-budget 0        disable 'thinking' on reasoning models
  --no-mmap                   load fully into RAM instead of mapping
  --mlock                     keep model locked in RAM
  --api-key mysecret          require a key (if exposing on LAN)
Run 'llama-server --help' for the full list.
estimate:
Rough VRAM estimate from the GGUF's tensor table:
weights on GPU + KV cache + compute buffer + mmproj + overhead.

Green < 85% of the card, yellow < 98%, red = probably won't fit.
After loading, compare with 'GPU buffers' in Status (actual).
copy: Copy the exact shell command (with the GPU env var) to the clipboard.
web: Open llama-server's built-in chat UI in your browser.
models_dir:
Folder scanned (recursively) for .gguf models.
mmproj files and extra split-model shards are hidden from the list.
server_bin:
Path to the ROCm (HIP) build of llama-server,
e.g. ~/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server
GPUs are detected with this one (--list-devices).
server_bin_vulkan:
Path to the Vulkan build of llama-server,
e.g. ~/llama.cpp/build-vulkan/bin/llama-server
(cmake -B build-vulkan -DGGML_VULKAN=ON). Picked per model with Build.
host:
Address servers listen on.
  127.0.0.1  this computer only (safe default)
  0.0.0.0    reachable from your LAN (consider --api-key)
left_port: Port used by the left pane for models with no saved port.
right_port: Port used by the right pane for models with no saved port.
chime:
Play a soft chime when a model finishes a response.

Only for requests that took at least the minimum time below, so
quick background calls (summaries, extensions) stay quiet.
Uses paplay / pw-play / aplay, whichever is installed.
chime_min_secs:
Only chime for requests that took at least this many seconds.
0 = chime after every request.
auto_load:
On startup, reload the model each pane was running last time,
with its saved options.

A pane is reloaded if its model was still running when the app
closed. Pressing Stop (or a crash) clears that, so a model you
stopped on purpose or that failed won't be auto-loaded again.
Either way, each pane re-selects its last used model on startup.
fit_margin_mib:
VRAM kept free when the Fit button picks a context size,
to absorb estimate error and desktop usage. Default 1536.
Too small and the driver may push the model out of VRAM.
overhead_mib:
Fixed amount added to every VRAM estimate for the GPU runtime.
Raise it if estimates are consistently below actual usage.
backend:
Inference engine for this pane.

  llama.cpp  GGUF files from the models folder (llama-server)
  KoboldCpp  the same GGUF files, run with KoboldCpp (ROCm or
             Vulkan build, chosen per model in the load options)
  vLLM       Hugging Face model folders (safetensors) from the
             vLLM models folder (vllm serve)
  Radiance   .rad containers (made with Convert…) and checkpoint
             folders from the Radiance models folder (radiance)

vLLM is EXPERIMENTAL: the memory estimate, load-time quant and
some model families (e.g. Gemma 4 KV sizing) aren't ironed out.

Each pane remembers its own backend, models and options.
Can't be changed while that pane's model is running.
v_ctx:
Context (--max-model-len): the longest prompt + reply one request
may use.

vLLM keeps ONE shared KV pool for all requests; this only sets the
per-request limit. vLLM refuses to start if a single request of
this length doesn't fit in the KV pool - press Fit to pick the
largest value that does.
v_fit:
Fit: set Context to the largest value whose KV cache fits in what
is left of the GPU memory budget after weights, runtime and
activation memory (GPU memory × card size).

Capped at the model's training context. After one real load the
estimate is calibrated from vLLM's own numbers.
gpu_util:
GPU memory (--gpu-memory-utilization): the share of each card vLLM
takes for itself, all of it allocated at startup.

Weights + runtime + activations come out of it; the rest becomes
the KV cache. 0.90 is safe; 0.95 gives more context.
The card must have this much FREE when loading (desktop, browser
and the other pane's model count against it).
kv_dtype:
KV cache type (--kv-cache-dtype).

  auto  same as the model (bf16/f16), full quality
  fp8   half the size: about twice the context. Small quality
        cost; RDNA4 has fp8 hardware. If a model produces
        garbage with it, go back to auto.
dtype:
Weight/activation precision (--dtype).

auto uses the model's own (usually bfloat16). Leave on auto.
quant:
Quantize at load (--quantization): shrink a 16-bit model's layer
weights while vLLM loads it. No separate step, but every launch
reads the full-size files.

  fp8_per_block   FP8 with 128x128 block scales - best quality
  fp8_per_tensor  FP8 with one scale per weight
  mxfp8           FP8 microscaling (W8A16 fallback off NVIDIA)
  mxfp4           4-bit: ~1/4 of the size, more quality loss

Embeddings and lm_head stay 16-bit (the estimate assumes so).
Support on RDNA4 depends on the vLLM build - if a launch fails
with a kernel/quantization error, try another or (none).
Disabled for models that are already quantized. For a permanent,
faster-loading copy use the Quantize tool in the top bar.
v_parallel:
Max sequences (--max-num-seqs): requests processed at once.

vLLM shares one KV pool, so context is NOT divided between them.
1 = requests queue (a background summary waits until your reply
is done). 2-4 = they run together and share the GPU.
Higher values also make vLLM capture more CUDA graphs at startup.
max_batched:
Batch tokens (--max-num-batched-tokens): prompt tokens processed
per step. 0 = vLLM's default (2048).

Bigger = faster long prompts but more activation memory, which
comes out of the KV cache (watch the estimate).
cpu_offload:
CPU offload (--cpu-offload-gb): GiB of weights per GPU kept in
system RAM and streamed over PCIe each step.

Lets a slightly-too-big model load, at a large speed cost.
Support on ROCm varies by vLLM build - 0 unless you need it.
eager:
Eager mode (--enforce-eager): skip torch.compile and CUDA graph
capture.

Much faster startup and a few GiB less memory, but slower
generation. Handy while testing settings.
text_only:
Text only: disable image/video/audio input for multimodal models
(--limit-mm-per-prompt with 0 for every modality).

vLLM then skips the vision encoder's memory profiling (and, in
recent builds, its weights), leaving more room for context.
reasoning:
Reasoning parser (--reasoning-parser): splits the model's
<think> block into a separate 'reasoning_content' field.

Pick the one for the model family (qwen3 for Qwen3/3.5,
glm45 for GLM-4.5/4.6, deepseek_r1 ...). (none) = leave the
thinking text inline. You can type any parser name your vLLM
build supports ('vllm serve --help' lists them).
v_relax_tpl:
Relaxed chat template: allow system messages anywhere in the chat.

Copies the model's own chat template (tokenizer_config.json or
chat_template.jinja), turns the 'system message must be first'
check into a normal system turn, saves it in ./templates and
passes it with --chat-template.
v_mtp:
Speculative decoding with the model's built-in MTP head
(--speculative-config method=mtp).

Only offered when config.json declares MTP layers (GLM-4.5,
DeepSeek, Qwen3-Next/3.5...). Same output, usually faster
generation; costs the MTP layer's weights and KV.
If your vLLM build wants a model-specific method name, put
--speculative-config '{...}' in Extra args instead.
v_mtp_n:
Speculative tokens (num_speculative_tokens): tokens the MTP head
proposes per step. 1-3 is typical; watch 'draft acceptance'.
v_extra:
Extra arguments passed straight to 'vllm serve', shell-style.

Examples:
  --generation-config vllm     ignore the model's sampling defaults
  --tool-call-parser hermes --enable-auto-tool-choice
  --api-key mysecret           require a key (if exposing on LAN)
  --swap-space 8               CPU swap for preempted requests
v_estimate:
vLLM takes GPU memory × card size at startup. Out of that:
weights + runtime/activation memory, and the rest is KV cache.

Green: Context fits with room to spare. Yellow: it fits but
barely. Red: vLLM will refuse to start (lower Context, raise
GPU memory, use fp8 KV, or span both GPUs).
After a load, 'GPU memory' in Status shows vLLM's real numbers.
v_web: Open this server's API docs page (vLLM has no chat UI).
v_dual_strategy:
How to span the model over both GPUs with vLLM:

  Auto Speed  the larger card alone if Context fits there,
              else the split with the most context
  Auto VRAM   the split that gives the most context
  Manual      choose split mode, ratio and device order

Pipeline split gives each card a block of layers (works with
mismatched cards; ratio set with VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION).
Tensor split halves every layer across both cards: the smaller
card caps it, and it syncs over PCIe on every layer.
v_dual_mode:
Split mode (Manual):
  pipeline  block of layers per card (--pipeline-parallel-size 2)
  tensor    every layer halved (--tensor-parallel-size 2); needs
            the KV head count to be even
v_dual_ts:
Layer ratio for a pipeline split (Manual), e.g. 3,7.
Blank = proportional to card size. Ignored for tensor.
vllm_bin:
Path to the 'vllm' program inside your vLLM venv,
e.g. ~/vllm/.venv/bin/vllm. The venv is used as-is; its
activate script does not need to be sourced.
vllm_models_dir:
Folder scanned for Hugging Face model folders (a config.json next
to *.safetensors), e.g. what 'hf download --local-dir' creates.
vllm_env:
Extra environment for vLLM, as KEY=VALUE pairs separated by spaces.
{models} is replaced by the vLLM models folder.

PYTHONPATH (amd_smi) and FLASH_ATTENTION_TRITON_AMD_ENABLE are
set automatically. Examples:
  HF_HUB_CACHE={models}/.hf-cache
  VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/some/folder TRITON_CACHE_DIR=/some/folder
vllm_left_port: Port used by the left pane for vLLM models with no saved port.
vllm_right_port: Port used by the right pane for vLLM models with no saved port.
kbuild:
Which build of the server runs this model (paths in Settings):

  ROCm    HIP build for AMD cards (usually the faster prompt
          processing)
  Vulkan  Vulkan build (no ROCm needed; often similar or better
          generation speed)

Stats and VRAM calibration are kept separately per build, so you
can switch back and forth to compare.
kquiet:
--quiet: keep prompts and replies out of the server log.
Speed lines (CtxLimit / Processed / Generated) are still shown.
Untick to see KoboldCpp's full Input/Output echo and live progress.
kobold_rocm_bin:
KoboldCpp ROCm build (single-file binary): the official rolling
build from github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/tag/rocm-rolling
(includes RX 9000 / RDNA4). Re-download it now and then - it is
updated in place; LLM Duo re-reads its options when the file changes.
Must be executable: chmod +x <file>
kobold_vulkan_bin:
KoboldCpp build with Vulkan, e.g. koboldcpp-linux-x64-nocuda
(or koboldcpp-linux-x64). Must be executable: chmod +x <file>
kobold_left_port: Port used by the left pane for KoboldCpp models with no saved port.
kobold_right_port: Port used by the right pane for KoboldCpp models with no saved port.
q_source:
16-bit model folder from the vLLM models folder.
Already-quantized models are not listed.
q_output:
Name of the new model folder (created next to the source in the
vLLM models folder). It shows up in vLLM panes when done.
q_ignore:
Extra module names to leave unquantized, as Python regular
expressions matched against the whole name, separated by spaces.

Always kept 16-bit: embeddings, lm_head, norms, MoE routers and
vision/audio parts. Use this only if vLLM refuses the result with
an 'unexpected key ...weight_scale' error naming a module, e.g.
  .*per_layer_.*
r_ctx:
Context (--max-model-len): the longest prompt + reply one request
may use. 0 = the model's own training context.

Radiance reserves nothing per request: this is the worst case its
KV pool is sized against. The pool never holds less than one
sequence of this length, so a context the card cannot hold makes
the start fail. Press Fit to use the largest one that fits.

Past the training context: --rope-scaling yarn:FACTOR in Extra args.
r_fit:
Fit: set Context to the largest value the KV pool holds for these
memory settings (KV cache, Max seqs, Batch tokens, Headroom,
placements, Host pool, Spec tokens), divided by Max seqs and
capped at the training context.

Radiance plans memory itself, so Fit asks it: the first time for a
set of memory settings it starts radiance briefly (a 'plan check'
on a spare port) and stops it as soon as the startup log states the
KV pool - usually a few seconds, before the weights are read.
After that (and after every real load) the figure is remembered
and Fit is instant. Press again while it runs to cancel.
r_kv:
KV cache type (--kv-cache-dtype).

  bf16     full precision - the engine's own default
  fp8      E4M3 with per-sequence descales: half the memory per
           token, a real (small) quantisation. LLM Duo's default.
  fp8_v4   K in fp8, V in int4: 25/32 of fp8's size
  k6_v4    K int6, V int4: 22/32 of fp8's size

fp8_v4 and k6_v4 exist only for Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next;
other models refuse them at startup.
r_parallel:
Max seqs (--max-num-seqs): sequences one step may carry at once.

Keep 1-2 for a single chat app. The engine's default of 256 is for
many-user serving: every sequence has a fixed cost (block tables,
sliding-window or recurrent state, a share of the activation arena),
which on a 32 GB card can leave only a few thousand tokens of
context. Fit divides the pool by this number.
r_batched:
Batch tokens (--max-num-batched-tokens): the largest step, so the
prefill chunk size. Default here 2048 (engine default 8192).

The activation arena grows with it and comes out of the KV pool.
On MoE models a bigger chunk prefills faster (each chunk sweeps all
experts once); 2048 is usually the sweet spot. Changing it changes
the exact output bits (a different batch shape).
r_spec:
Spec tokens (--num-speculative-tokens): draft depth for the draft
head inside the container (an MTP head, or one merged with
Convert's Draft model).

  auto  the drafter's own operating point (default)
  0     speculation off
  N     a fixed depth (the ceiling with Draft window = adaptive)

Judge it by step time / generation speed, not acceptance.
r_draft_window:
Draft window (--draft-window).

  fixed     draft Spec tokens every step
  adaptive  follow each sequence's acceptance and the measured step
            cost; Spec tokens is the ceiling. Code/JSON keep drafting
            deep, prose stops early. Serial draft heads only (the
            startup log says when it can't apply).
r_headroom:
Headroom (--gpu-headroom-mib): VRAM Radiance leaves unclaimed on
every card (default 96 MiB). It claims the rest at startup - a
full VRAM reading is normal and does not mean the context is full.

Raise it when the startup log warns (a W line names the value) or
when something else on that card (the desktop on the 9070 XT) needs
room; too little can make a kernel's first launch crash the server.
r_vision:
Vision tower (--vision-tower-placement).

  (default)  the engine's choice: on the card
  vram       on the card
  ram        pinned in system RAM, read once per image over PCIe
             (≈55 ms per image); its VRAM goes to the KV pool

ram is refused for models without a vision tower.
r_embed:
Embedding (--embedding-placement): where the token embedding lives.

  (default)  ram for most models (pinned host memory, read in
             place - costs no VRAM)
  vram       on the card (models whose head is tied to it keep it
             there anyway)
r_placement:
Placement (--placement): how weights are placed.

  auto           the engine decides (default)
  all_vram       every weight on the card
  layer_offload  whole layers in host memory
  expert_tiered  MoE: experts that don't fit live in the pinned
                 Host pool and are read over PCIe; the KV pool lends
                 its unused blocks back to the experts

With a lending cache (auto / expert_tiered) a bigger Host pool
gives the KV pool more room.
r_host_pool:
Host pool (--host-pool-mib): pinned system RAM for weights that
don't stay on the card (MoE experts). 0 = off.

At --tp 2 every card pins its own pool. The amdgpu driver caps
all pinned memory at about RAM minus 1/64 and 1.5 GiB.
r_prefix_mib:
Prefix cache (--prefix-cache-mib): copy finished conversations'
KV cache to system RAM, up to this many MiB, so a later turn (or a
switch back to another chat) resumes without re-reading its whole
prompt. 0 = off (only what fits in VRAM is kept).
r_prefill_span:
Prefill span (--prefill-span N): a prefill alone in its step may
carry N checkpoint intervals at once (needs Batch tokens of N
intervals). Mostly for hybrid / MoE models at long context; models
without an interval grid (Gemma 4) span nothing. 1 = off.
r_reasoning:
Reasoning (--reasoning-effort): default reasoning_effort for chat
requests that don't send one. (default) = the chat template's own
(Qwen3.8's is xhigh, which can spend a short max_tokens entirely
inside <think>). A request that names one wins.
r_tp_wire:
Tensor parallel wire (--tp-wire), Dual GPU mode only.

  exact  bf16 all-reduce (default)
  wht6   a lossy 6-bit rotated payload, 2.4x smaller over PCIe;
         messages under 128 KiB stay exact, so single-stream
         decode stays exact and prefill is compressed.

Radiance has no layer (pipeline) split: Dual GPU mode runs --tp 2,
every layer halved across the cards with an all-reduce per layer.
The KV pool is sized to the tighter card, so a 32 GB + 16 GB pair
often holds LESS context than the 32 GB card alone, and PCIe 3.0 x8
links make every step pay for the exchange.
r_extra:
Extra arguments passed straight to radiance, shell-style.

Examples:
  --temp 0.7 --min-p 0.05          sampler defaults
  --rope-scaling yarn:2             past the training context
  --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'
  --api-key mysecret                require a key
  --live                            the live terminal view
  -v                                debug logging
Unknown options stop the server at startup (radiance --help lists them).
r_estimate:
Radiance claims the whole card at startup (less Headroom) and splits
it between resident weights and a paged KV pool itself, so this
is not a byte-by-byte estimate. It shows the container size per
card and the KV pool Radiance reported for these memory settings
(from Fit's plan check or a real load), and whether Context × Max
seqs fits it.

Green: fits. Yellow: unmeasured, or the pool holds fewer
full-length sessions than Max seqs. Red: Context does not fit.
r_web:
Open Radiance's built-in dashboard (http://host:port/dashboard): step time, throughput,
KV cache, sessions and the resolved kernel graph. The chat page is at /, the API at /v1,
and the raw figures at /stats, /sessions, /server_info and /metrics.
radiance_bin:
Path to the radiance binary, e.g. ~/radiance/build/bin/radiance.
rad-info and rad-convert are looked for in the same folder.
radiance_home:
RADIANCE_HOME: the folder with kernels/, architectures/ and
quantizers/ (the engine's plugins, not models), e.g.
~/radiance/build/radiance_home. Passed on Radiance's own command
line only - never put it (or HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES) in ~/.bashrc.
radiance_models_dir:
Folder scanned for .rad containers and checkpoint folders
(config.json + safetensors, served at their own precision).
Convert… writes its containers here.
radiance_recipes_dir:
Radiance's recipes folder (e.g. ~/radiance/data/recipes). Convert…
lists the *.recipe files found here each time it opens, so new
recipes from a Radiance update appear without changing LLM Duo.
radiance_env:
Extra environment variables for Radiance, KEY=VALUE separated by
spaces, e.g.  RADIANCE_LOG=debug  or  AMD_LOG_LEVEL=1
{models} is replaced by the Radiance models folder.
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES and RADIANCE_HOME are set by LLM Duo.
radiance_left_port:
Default port for a Radiance model in the left pane (Radiance's own
default is 8000). The same as llama.cpp's by default, so chat apps
keep working when you switch backends.
radiance_right_port: Default port for a Radiance model in the right pane.
c_source:
The checkpoint to convert: a Hugging Face model folder (config.json
+ *.safetensors), a .safetensors file or an index.json. The list
shows folders found in the vLLM and Radiance models folders; type or
Browse… for any other.
c_recipe:
The quantisation recipe from Radiance's recipes folder. A finetune
uses its base model's recipe (e.g. any Gemma 4 31B finetune -> the
bf16 one). The recipe's header comment is shown below and any
--set keys it names are filled in.

(none) keeps every weight as the checkpoint stores it - only bf16,
f16, f32 and block-scaled FP8 are accepted that way.
c_output:
The container to write: a name (placed in the Radiance models
folder) or a full path. Ends in .rad.
c_sets:
--set KEY=VALUE (space separated): metadata written into the
container and seen when it is converted and served - e.g. the
quantization_config keys some recipes need to select the right
serving plugin.

Filled in automatically from the recipe's header, or - for a bf16
checkpoint converted with a recipe that quantises it - with the keys
that select the family's quantised serving plugin (Qwen3.8: the fp8
set; Gemma 4 31B: compressed-tensors). Anything you type yourself
is never replaced.
c_draft:
--draft-model DIR: merge a drafter that ships as its own repository
(DSpark, DFlash2) into the container. An MTP head inside the
checkpoint needs nothing.
c_maxctx:
--max-ctx N: the context bound the graph is declared at (default:
the checkpoint's training context). Some models size buffers by it.
c_env:
Environment for rad-convert, KEY=VALUE separated by spaces. Recipes
that calibrate (gptq calib=$CALIB) need CALIB=<dir>; an unset
variable is refused.
c_extra:
Extra rad-convert arguments, e.g.
  --imatrix FILE            llama.cpp imatrix (expert profile, weighting)
  --quant 'PAT=QUANT:k=v'   a rule ahead of the recipe's
  --reuse OLD.rad           copy weights an earlier container holds
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8      the cache width declare runs at
c_plan:
Plan only (--plan-only -v): declare, plan every weight's encoding,
print the plan and stop - nothing is written. Use it to check a
recipe against a checkpoint first.
c_gpu:
Which card rad-convert may use (HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES, on its own command line only).

  (auto)     the card a Radiance pane uses, else the largest card
  all cards  every card visible
  a card     only that one

Keeping it to one card leaves the other free for a running model.
llama_api_key:
API key for llama-server (--api-key). Clients must send
Authorization: Bearer <key>; /health stays open. The built-in web UI asks for it.

Leave empty for no key. Applies from the next Load. LLM Duo's own status polling sends it
automatically; the command shown in the log and in error reports hides it as ••••
(Copy command includes it, so the copied line runs as is).
kobold_password:
Password for KoboldCpp (--password). API clients send it as
Authorization: Bearer <password>; KoboldAI Lite asks for it.

Leave empty for no key. Applies from the next Load. LLM Duo's own status polling sends it
automatically; the command shown in the log and in error reports hides it as ••••
(Copy command includes it, so the copied line runs as is).
vllm_api_key:
API key for vLLM (--api-key). Protects the /v1 endpoints; clients send
Authorization: Bearer <key>.

Leave empty for no key. Applies from the next Load. LLM Duo's own status polling sends it
automatically; the command shown in the log and in error reports hides it as ••••
(Copy command includes it, so the copied line runs as is).
radiance_api_key:
API key for Radiance (--api-key). Every request except /health, /v1/health,
/ping and the dashboard page needs Authorization: Bearer <key> (or X-Api-Key,
for Anthropic clients); the dashboard asks for it once and remembers it.

Leave empty for no key. Applies from the next Load. LLM Duo's own status polling sends it
automatically; the command shown in the log and in error reports hides it as ••••
(Copy command includes it, so the copied line runs as is).
mtp_dev:
Which card runs the MTP drafter in Dual GPU mode (--spec-draft-device).

  (auto)  the card with the last layers and the output layer (normally the
          larger card), or the one card of a single-GPU plan
  a card  that card - e.g. the 9070 XT, to leave the R9700's VRAM to context

The estimate moves the drafter's size to the card you pick. Putting it on
the card WITHOUT the output layer adds a hand-off per draft step, which
can cost speed - compare t/s in History.
A --spec-draft-device in Extra args overrides this.
